Environment autocorrelated in space and time

Source: R/landscape.R
env_space_time.Rd

Simulates the changing environment of Thompson et al. (2020): a Gaussian random field over space and time with exponential covariance, held constant during a burn-in, rescaled to [0, 1] and converted to ranks. Unlike env_over_time(), which gives each site its own AR(1) series, sites close together change together.

Usage

env_space_time(
  landscape,
  n_steps,
  burn_in = 200,
  spatial_scale = 50,
  temporal_scale = 500,
  ranks = TRUE,
  min_range = 0.6,
  n_features = 2000
)

Arguments

landscape

An mc_landscape with coordinates, from landscape_grid() or landscape_points(), or a two-column matrix or data frame of site coordinates.

n_steps

Number of steps, burn-in included: one whole number, larger than burn_in.

burn_in

Number of initial steps with a constant environment: one whole number, 0 or more.

spatial_scale, temporal_scale

Scales \(a_s\) (in units of the coordinates) and \(a_t\) (in steps) of the exponential covariance: each one number greater than 0.

ranks

TRUE or FALSE. If TRUE, convert the environment to ranks over all sites and steps, as in their code; if FALSE, keep the rescaled field.

min_range

Minimum range of the rescaled environment at the first step after the burn-in; the field is redrawn until it is exceeded: one number in [0, 1). Use 0 to accept the first draw.

n_features

Number of cosine waves of the spectral method: one whole number, 1 or more.

Value

Matrix with one row per site and one column per step, with values in [0, 1], for the env_time argument of simulate_metacommunity(). Multiply it to put it on the scale of the traits.

Details

The covariance between two site-steps is \(\exp(-\sqrt{(d/a_s)^2 + (\Delta t/a_t)^2})\), with \(d\) the distance between the sites, \(\Delta t\) the number of steps between them, and \(a_s\) and \(a_t\) the spatial and temporal scales. The authors' code (Meta_com_framework v1.0, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.3708350) draws this field with RandomFields::RFsimulate(RMexp(scale = 500)) on coordinates multiplied by 10 and steps in units of one, which gives the defaults \(a_s = 50\) and \(a_t = 500\) for patches with coordinates between 1 and 100. RandomFields is no longer on CRAN, so the field is drawn here by the spectral method (random Fourier features): the sum of n_features cosine waves whose frequencies are drawn from the spectral density of the exponential covariance, a multivariate Student t with one degree of freedom. The covariance is exact in expectation, and the field is close to Gaussian for large n_features.

As in their code, the field is drawn for the steps after the burn-in, the environment of the first step after it is repeated over the burn-in, the whole field is rescaled to [0, 1] and redrawn until the environment of that first step spans more than min_range, and the values of all sites and steps, burn-in included, are converted to ranks, so that the environment is uniform on [0, 1]. The field is not on a torus, even when the landscape is.

References

Thompson, P. L., Guzman, L. M., De Meester, L., Horváth, Z., Ptacnik, R., Vanschoenwinkel, B., Viana, D. S., & Chase, J. M. (2020). A process-based metacommunity framework linking local and regional scale community ecology. Ecology Letters, 23, 1314–1329. doi:10.1111/ele.13568

See also

Other landscapes: dispersal_kernel(), env_over_time(), env_pulse(), env_river(), env_seasonal(), landscape_grid(), landscape_implicit(), landscape_matrix(), landscape_points(), landscape_river(), river_covariance(), river_floods(), river_network()

Examples

set.seed(1)
xy <- cbind(x = runif(30, 1, 100), y = runif(30, 1, 100))
e <- env_space_time(xy, n_steps = 600, burn_in = 100)
matplot(t(e[1:5, ]), type = "l", lty = 1, xlab = "step", ylab = "environment")
